summary: Zhengyan Fan is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. Fan was a PhD researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026) and served on the Ghent University faculty (attested 2026).
Zhenhua (1922–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tianning Temple (1947) and under Yinshun (1952). He served as manager at Fuyan Buddhist Institute (attested 1992).

Zhihua Yao specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from Boston University under Malcolm David Eckel (~1997–2002) and held positions at the University of Hong Kong (~2003–2005) and The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2005).

Zhiru Ng specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. She earned an MA at the University of Michigan under Luis O. Gómez and a PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello.

Zhiru Shi works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Arizona under Robert M. Gimello and held appointments at Pomona College (attested 2007–2014) and Fo Guang University (attested 2026).

Zhiyi Yang specializes in Sinology. After undergraduate studies at Peking University, she earned her PhD at Princeton University under Martin Kern, and has held posts at the International Consortium for Research in the Humanities and Goethe University Frankfurt (attested 2015).

Zhonghui Cui specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. She completed an MA at SOAS University of London, earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong, and served as a teaching consultant there (attested 2013).
Zhongpei Zhang (1934–2017) was a Sinologist and archaeologist who studied under Bai Su (~1952–1956). He served as director of the Palace Museum from ~1987 to 1991.

Zhongxin Jiang (1942–2002) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University under Xianlin Ji (~1960–1968) and held posts at Peking University, the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978–2002), and Soka University's IRIAB (~1998–1999).
Zhuan Dao (1871–1943) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tongzhi. He founded Poo Thor Jee in 1911 and Kong Meng San Phor Kark See Monastery in 1920.
Zijie Li is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (attested 2015). In 2015, Li held a DC special researcher position at the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.

Zoltán Gombocz (1877–1935) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at the Berzsenyi Dániel Evangélikus Gimnázium until 1895 and at Eötvös Loránd University from 1895 to 1900.

Zong Rinpoche (1905–1984) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies figure who studied at Ganden and Gyuto monasteries under Trijang Rinpoche and Dechen Nyingpo. He served as abbot of Ganden Monastery (1937–1946) and rector of CIHTS (1967–1971).

Zsóka Gelle (b. 1967) specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Berzsenyi Dániel Teacher Training College, Eötvös Loránd University, and the University of Vienna, and held posts at Dharma Gate Buddhist College and Eötvös Loránd University (2014–2016).
Zuicho Tachibana (1890–1968) was a scholar in Iranian/Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He studied under Kozui Otani (~1903–1914) and Edward Denison Ross (~1908–1909).

Zuiei Ito (1942–2020) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned doctorates from the University of Tokyo and Waseda University. He was a professor at Rissho University (1980–2013) and lectured at Tokyo, Waseda, and Shinshu Universities.

Zuigan Goto (1879–1965) was a Buddhist and religious studies figure. He studied at the University of Tokyo (1903–1906) and under Sokatsu Shaku (~1900–1914), later serving as president of Hanazono University (1932).

Zuiho Yamaguchi (1926–2023) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and EPHE under Jacques Bacot and Rolf Alfred Stein. He held posts at CNRS, Toyo Bunko, Tokyo University, and Nagoya University.

Zuiryu Nakamura (1915–1995) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, studying under Susumu Yamaguchi and Kenryu Tsukinowa. He became a professor at Rissho University in 1945 and served as director of the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

Zumo Zhou (1914–1995) was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at Peking University under Luo Changpei. He held appointments at Academia Sinica, Fu Jen Catholic University (~1940–1952), and Peking University as associate professor (1947) and professor (1950).
